description:
FILED s450 (Fable, round-9 batch legs).  Companion op/exec.t 23/2 -> 22/3: perl row 17, `ok($! == 2 or $! =~ /\bno\b.*\bfile/i or ...)` at exec.t:114 -- the errno check following the `system { "lskdfj" } "lskdfj"` statement whose form ABORTS in both trees ("Couldn't execute", the pre-existing indirect-object-system family).  REAL MOVE: parallel and serial agree.

MEASUREMENTS TAKEN (do not redo):
  * Bisected: f937afd (pre-V) = 23/2; fd94dba (#541 only) = 23/2; merged (9e11ce0 s/// commit in) = 22/3.  The s/// commit owns it.
  * Plain/interp/e-modifier s/// do NOT clobber $! (probed: $!=2 survives all three, both trees).
  * The minimal `system {} ` shape aborts IDENTICALLY on both trees; the row only exists under p-load-with-recovery (suite mode), so plain runpcl cannot reach it.
  * Shapes in range: exec.t:72 has `s/\n\n/\n/g` (constant replacement); exec.t:78 `local $TODO = ... if $Is_VMS` is one of #541's 20 A/B hunks but the #541-only tree is CLEAN; test.pl:1411 has `s/^#\s*\U$what\E.../ /m` (case shift in the PATTERN side, which #522 did not touch -- verify).

NEXT DISCRIMINATOR (the cheap one not yet taken): capture the file's own diag -- row 17's `unless` prints `$! eq %d, '%s'` -- by re-running the suite runner with the child's raw TAP kept (add a temp PCL_SUITE_KEEP env to tools/run-perl-suite.pl or instrument p-load-with-recovery to tee), on both trees; the two printed errno values name the mechanism.  Suspects, in order: the widened `_replacement_interpolates` gate routing some test.pl replacement onto the lambda path whose cl-ppcre non-simple call perturbs *p-stored-errno*; a case-shift PATTERN interaction at test.pl:1411.

BAR: the diag values captured both trees; the mechanism named; either fixed (row back to ok) or the divergence explained perl-shaped; the exec.t snapshot row restored 23/2 or re-spliced with the true cause.

DONE s451w (commit 477fc93).  MECHANISM: s450v's #521 _undelimit (a fragment lifted out of a dq construct carries the ESCAPED delimiter, so \" -> ") ran on EVERY fragment.  A heredoc, a qq{}, a backtick command and a <...> glob reach parse_interpolated_string wrapped in a SYNTHETIC "..." token over their RAW text, where \" is the reference operator followed by a string -- so <<`H` with l${\"s"} became ""s" (unparseable) and the interpolation went EMPTY: ls -> l.  NOT *p-stored-errno*, NOT the case-shift pattern at test.pl:1411, NOT _replacement_interpolates -- both suspects in this task are WRONG, do not retry them.  The row that flipped is perl row 32 (<<`` respects overrides), not row 17: the $! row is inside the aborted system{} form and PCL never emits it; the runner's number-fallback join is what made it LOOK like row 17.  FIX: _delim_escapes_dquote asked of $origin_tok (the ORIGINAL document token); the glob and backtick sites were passing their synthetic wrapper and now pass the real token.  op/exec.t 22/3 -> 23/2.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL; emission A/B 1036 files = ONE diff (op/exec.t's two ${\"..."} sites regaining (p-backslash ...)).  Guard Pl/t/regexp-subst-01.t +1 row (8 shapes).  INSTRUMENT ADDED: PCL_SUITE_KEEP=DIR in tools/run-perl-suite.pl.  Residue #702 (backtick heredoc never executed) and #703 (readpipe override ignored) -- exec.t row 32 passes only because those two cancel.
subject: op/exec.t row 17 (the $! sanity check after the aborted `system {}` form) flipped ok -> not-ok with s450v's s/// commit -- one row, mechanism NOT yet isolated; the discriminating measurements taken are recorded here
